newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Redland long term rating to A.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Redland long term rating to A.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Tuesday it had downgraded Redland Plc's long-term rating to A from A plus.
It affirmed Redland's short-term rating of A1, IBCA said.
Redland is a UK based manufacturer of building materials - mainly roof tiles and aggregates - with a large international presence, IBCA said.

"Although Redland's geographical diversity and strong market shares offer a degree of protection against the cyclicality of regional construction markets, the reliance on Germany is of concern," IBCA said.

The German construction market, which accounts for over half of Redland's group profits, has been losing momentum since 1995 and is expected to slow further due to budgetary tightening ahead of European monetary union, IBCA said.
"Redland management appear to have underestimated the magnitude of the downturn and has twice been proved wrong in predicting a return to higher demand," IBCA said.
Severe winter weather in early 1996 also had a negative impact on sales. More recently, the strength of sterling has been reducing the group's foreign profits, IBCA said.
Following the sale of Redland's bricks businesses in 1996, the aggregates division now represents the group's only non-roofing activity, IBCA said.

Redland Aggregates enjoys strong market positions although returns are poor. The general reduction in government spending across Europe over the next few years will result in the scaling back of infrastructure projects and, consequently, lower requirements for aggregates, IBCA said.
"The increasing business pressure on Redland has begun to affect its financial structure, evidenced by a deterioration in coverages," IBCA said.

"Net gearing reached 50 percent at June 1996; although interim gearing is normally higher than at year end due to the seasonality of the building cycle, this figure has increased significantly since June 1994," IBCA said.
"Debt will have reduced at fiscal year end 1996 due to proceeds received from the sale of bricks operations," IBCA said.
"However, the latter is earmarked for expansion in Asia Pacific and is likely to be reinvested in the near future," IBCA said.
